newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan President Lee may meet Dalai Lama - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan President Lee may meet Dalai Lama - paper.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui may meet with the Dalai Lama despite an expected protest from China, when the exiled Tibetan Buddhist leader visits the island later in March, the United Evening News reported on Sunday.
The newspaper quoted unidentified sources as saying Lee may meet unofficially with the Dalai Lama before the Tibetan god-king leaves Taiwan on March 27.
Lee's office has denied that it has set any meeting between the president and the Dalai Lama, but declined to say whether it was trying to arrange a session.

China on Friday warned Taiwan, which it has regarded as a renegade province since the two sides split after their civil war in 1949, not to fan separatist sentiment during the Dalai Lama's March 22 visit to the island.
Taipei has maintained that the Dalai Lama's visit would be purely religious in nature and would not include official contacts.

The Dalai Lama, who won the 1989 Nobel Peace Prize for his non-violent campaign for autonomy for his Himalayan homeland, was invited to Taiwan by the island's private Buddhist Association of the Republic of China.
China has made strenuous efforts to neutralise the Dalai Lama's influence abroad since he went into exile in 1959 after an abortive uprising against Beijing's rule.
Chinese troops in 1950 had moved in to replace the centuries-old Buddhist theocracy with control from Beijing.
The Dalai Lama, revered at home as a god-king, advocates non-violent resistance to Chinese domination and says he wants autonomy for Tibet.
Beijing has maintained that Tibet is an integral part of China, just as Taiwan must be brought under the mainland's eventual rule.
Taiwan has said it wants to re-unify with the mainland but insists it has the right to conduct foreign affairs during the current separation.
